blocks.text:
Explanation:- The meaning of the hadith is that the more the outward and inward aspects of the Salah conform to the Sunnah, the more reward and good one receives.
(Badhl al-Majhud)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ﵄ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ قَالَ: الصَّلَاةُ مَثْنَي مَثْنَي تَشَهَّدُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، وَتَضَرَّعُ، وَتَخَشَّعُ، وتَمَسْكَنُ ثُمَّ تُقَنِّعُ يَدَيْكَ يَقُولُ تَرْفَعُهُمَا إِلَي رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقْبِلاً بِبُطُونِهَما وَجْهَكَ تَقُولُ: يَارَبِّ يَارَبِّ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ فَهُوَكَذَاوكَذاَ.
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Fadl ibn Abbas (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said, “When praying in units of two rak'ahs, recite the “Tashahhud' at the end of every two rak'ahs. Pray expressing your helplessness, with humility, lowliness and calm. After finishing the Salah, raise both hands up to the chest with the palms facing the face and make Du'a to your Lord. Make Du'a saying (Ya Rabbi, Ya Rabbi) “O my Lord! O my Lord!'. The Salah of one who does not do this is a deficient Salah (in terms of reward and recompense).”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: لَا يَزَالُ اللهُ مُقْبِلاً عَلَي الْعَبْدِ فِي صَلَاتِهِ مَالَمْ يَلْتَفِتْ، فَإِذَا صَرَفَ وَجْهَهُ انْصَرَفَ عَنْهُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه النسائي باب التشديد في الالتفات في الصلاة رقم:١١٩٦
blocks.tamil_translation: “As long as the servant does not turn his attention elsewhere in Salah, Allah too turns His attention towards the servant. If the servant turns his attention away from the Salah, Allah too turns His attention away from the servant.” Hazrat Abu Dharr (RA)
